headline: India joins global rate-tightening wave with first hike in nearly 4 years - AOL
summary: The Reserve Bank of India raised its benchmark repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5% on Wednesday, its first increase in nearly four years. The move comes amid broader global rate tightening.
why: The RBI sets India's benchmark lending rate, which influences borrowing costs, bank lending and the rupee. Rate decisions are closely watched by investors in Indian equities and bonds.
why_moved: The RBI's rate increase tightens monetary policy by raising the benchmark cost of borrowing, which typically pressures rate-sensitive assets.
